title: Workload Adaptive Presets — Lab Notes
body:
Context:
This is a working lab doc for the "workload adaptive presets" concept — a lightweight UX in Console that suggests and applies bunded configuration presets (batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profile) per-route or per-model based on recent traffic patterns. Goal is a low-friction way for engineers and infra teams to get measurable cost reduction without manual tuning.

Goals / success signals (rough):
- users can preview estimated cost and p99 latency impact before applying a preset (primary).
- average token cost reduced by >= 10% for stateful chat workloads in the first 30 days on pilot routes.
- low incidence of customer-visible quality regressions (sampled human eval pass rate > 95%).
- adoption: at least 15 internal pilot routes during the experiment window.

Hypotheses we want to test:
H1: Most customers will accept a single "Safe Economy" preset for long-context chat routes if a simple A/B preview shows no sample-quality regression.
H2: Users care more about predictable tail latency than tiny avg cost savings — so UI needs explicit p95/p99 estimates and rollback guardrails.
H3: Quantization suggestions are sticky only for deterministic generation use-cases; for open-ended chat customers, caching+batching gives more value per risk.

Telemetry & estimation model notes:
- Inputs: recent 7/14/30-day request histograms (seq len distribution, typical context length, KV cache hit rates if enabled), model variant, hw type.
- Output: estimated delta for tokens/sec cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, and a 90% confidence interval for quality risk (based on past evals of similar quant profiles + prompt similarity heuristic).
- Data flags: if insufficient telemetry (<500 requests/day), mark as "experimental estimate" and show larger uncertainty.

Preset taxonomy (working):
- Safe Economy (low quantization aggression, modest batching thresholds, prefer small prefix caching window)
- Aggressive Savings (INT8-style quant + aggressive batching + long prefix caching)
- Latency-Optimized (minimal batching, larger instance type, no quant)
- Stateful-Caching (KV-first, keep-hot-prefixes, ideal for chat-history heavy workloads)

Sketch / wireframe ideas (textual):
- Top-level: Presets panel on route config page. Small card for each preset: name, 3-line bullets (cost delta, delta latency, quality risk), quick apply button, preview simulation button.
- Preview modal: left = simulation controls (time window, simulated RPS, sample prompt set), center = charts (cost over time, p50/p99 latency bands, cache hit heatmap), right = sample generations (side-by-side baseline vs preset on 4 golden prompts).
- Small inline change indicator: "Estimated -12% cost, +20ms p99, quality risk: low". Clicking the risk pill expands to show which prompts degraded in the sample.

Interaction flow (day 1 pilot):
1) User clicks "Suggest presets" on route, system analyzes recent week of traffic.
2) UI surfaces recommended preset(s) with 'confidence' and "preview" CTA.
3) User runs preview simulation (default 1000 simulated requests or use live replay).
4) User clicks "Apply to route" — UI performs a canary rollout with built-in guardrails (traffic slice, monitor quality signals for 30 minutes).
5) If automated regressions detected (quality-signal threshold or latency threshold), system rolls back and notifies owner.

Mini-UX experiments to try (MVP -> M1 -> M2):
- MVP: single recommended preset + preview + apply with manual canary size selection (10/50/100).
- M1: show cost/latency deltas inline for each preset and allow quick schedule (apply at X:00).
- M2: multi-presets A/B compare with automatic selection by traffic segment and auto-fallback rules.

Evaluation / quality safeguards:
- Must run sample generation comparison for 10 seeded prompts and 10 random recent prompts. Show exact diffs; allow user to mark "acceptable" or "unacceptable" per prompt.
- Integrate with eval harness (applies rouge/bertscore or embed-sim threshold) and a human-in-the-loop review flow for first 5 deployments per customer.

Backlog / immediate tasks (assignments tentative):
- [ ] Telemetry: expose per-route seq-length histogram + KV hit estimation (Miguel).
- [ ] Estimator service: quick offline estimator prototype to return cost/latency deltas (Evan).
- [ ] UI: draft preview modal mock + mobile fallback (Priya).
- [ ] Guardrails spec: define automatic rollback thresholds and owner notification flow (Jordan).
- [ ] UX copy: microcopy for risk/uncertainty pills (product writing).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What exact confidence level do we show? 90% CI seems understandable, but product may prefer single-point conservative delta.
- How to measure "quality risk" automatically without massive labeled data? (possible approach: prompt-sim embedding divergence + historical evals mapped to quant profiles).
- Should presets be first-class resources (reusable across routes) or per-route suggestions only? Tradeoffs: discovery vs accidental cross-route impact.
- Canary timing defaults: 30 minutes vs 4 hours — shorter may miss slow drift, longer increases blast radius.

Notes from quick hallway UX test (2 engineers):
- "Preview is the killer feature" — both testers liked seeing side-by-side samples more than charts.
- They want an explicit "undo" button and a non-obvious "safety slider" (turn down aggressiveness from recommended preset).
- Preference for short textual rationale: "Why this preset?" (one-line explanation).

Edge cases to handle:
- Low-traffic routes: offer sandbox simulation only, warn about estimator uncertainty.
- Multi-model routes (routing by input): show composite preset or suggest per-model variants.
- Live inference constraints (e.g., GPU memory) — presets must validate against the deployment pool capacity.

Possible UI microcopy snippets (drafts):
- Preset card subtitle: "Estimated: -12% avg token cost • +20ms p99 • Quality risk: Low"
- Preview CTA: "Run simulated preview (1k requests)"
- Canary CTA: "Apply as canary (10% traffic, auto-monitor)"

Next-step experiment plan (2 weeks):
Week 1: implement offline estimator + lightweight preview modal with static sample set. Run internal pilot on 5 routes.
Week 2: collect pilot signals, iterate presets taxonomy, add canary rollouts and rollback automation.

Appendix: quick ASCII wireframe for preview modal (super-rough)

[ Preview Modal ]
| Controls | Charts (cost + latency bands) | Samples (baseline | preset) |
| Time window: [7d] [14d] [30d] | cost: --- area chart --- | Prompt 1: BASELINE / PRESET |
| Simulation size: [1k] [5k] | p99: 320ms -> 340ms | Prompt 2: BASELINE / PRESET |

——
Unresolved/Ongoing: keep this doc as the single place for quick notes. Move to a formal spec once the pilot data shows stable deltas.

Quick contact: Jordan Lee (product), slack: @jordanl — leave comments inline or add to linked Linear ticket.
